t: #3502 Minimum Cost to Reach Every Position
o: You start at position n and move left by swapping. Paying cost[i] lets you pass person i while moving forward; once you are to the left of someone, they can swap with you for free. So to reach position i, you never need to pay anyone to the right of i, and among people 0..i you only ever need to pay the cheapest one — pay them once, then free swaps carry you anywhere left of them. Hence answer[i] = min(cost[0..i]). Example 1 gives prefix minima [5,3,3,1,1,1]; Example 2 gives all 1s since cost[0]=1.
k: Once you pay person j, everyone right of j swaps with you for free.
answer[i] depends only on the prefix minimum of cost[0..i].

a.i: Scan left to right maintaining the minimum cost seen so far; that minimum is exactly the answer for the current index.
s: For each i, update best = min(best, cost[i]) and append best.

a.i: For each target position independently, scan the whole prefix and take its minimum — the direct translation of the observation.
s: For each i from 0 to n-1, compute min(cost[0..i]) by a nested loop.
a.t: O(n²) — each prefix is rescanned; fine for n ≤ 100.

w: Always present the prefix-minimum solution; the brute force is only a stepping stone. Pitfall: thinking you must pay every person you pass — paying the cheapest person in the prefix once suffices because backward swaps are free. Follow-up: what if backward swaps also had costs (then it becomes a shortest-path problem).
